children: The U.S. Department of Agriculture will proceed with a plan to resume livestock imports from Mexico at a large New Mexico port next week following a detection of New World screwworm in the state, the agency said on X on Friday.
Screwworm infested a horse in Grant County, New Mexico, in the southwest corner of the state near the Mexican border, USDA said on Thursday.
The U.S. halted livestock imports from Mexico last year to keep out screwworm but began to resume trade last month at an Arizona port as part of a phased reopening plan.
